clue.text: Referring to landlord in Lincoln, say

parts.note: re means concerning or with reference to
a publican is the landlord of a pub

explanation.surface: Someone asks about the landlord of a pub in the city of Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln looks like the English cathedral city, but it is Abraham Lincoln, US president.
explanation.definitionFit: Abraham Lincoln was the first US president from that party, so he is an example of one.

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the run of words disaster areas

explanation.surface: Something that hardly ever turns up where catastrophe has struck.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seldom seen is uncommon, an exact synonym.

clue.text: A superintendent finally in position to calm down

indicators.note: in says the A and final letter are put inside the word for position

parts.note: a place is a position

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of superintendent

explanation.surface: A police superintendent at last takes up a post where they can settle things down.
explanation.definitionFit: To pacify an angry person is to calm them down, a transitive synonym.

clue.text: A rye 'Webster's' set out as a source of vitamin B

indicators.note: set out means arranged afresh, so the letters of the quoted words are laid out in a new order

explanation.surface: A rye whisky called Webster's is promoted as rich in vitamin B.
explanation.definitionFit: The fungus used in brewing is a dietary supplement rich in B vitamins, so it is one such source.

clue.text: At work, that man's enthralled by right- winger on paper

parts.note: in can mean at work, as in 'is the boss in today?'

indicators.note: enthralled by means held captive inside the word for a right-winger

parts.note: a Tory is a member of Britain's right-wing Conservative Party
that man is a male pronoun, he; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A man at the office is captivated by a conservative politician, at least in writing.
explanation.walkthrough: TORY is a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Something true on paper holds as a matter of principle but perhaps not in practice, an idiomatic synonym.

indicators.note: moving signals that the letters of statue are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A clever statue that moves, a nice paradox.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewd and sharp-witted mean the same, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Singer opening in Berlin — when? First of September

indicators.note: opening in is read as making an opening in the pair of initials, so the word for when goes between them
First of picks the initial letter of each of Berlin and September

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A singer asks when Berlin's season opens, and is told the start of September.
explanation.walkthrough: Read straight, this is B (opening in Berlin), then AS (when), then S (First of September); the parse shows the same letters as the two initials with AS between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A singer with the lowest male voice is called by this name, so it is a type of singer.

clue.text: Sign erected in an English plant

indicators.note: in says the upturned sign goes inside an
erected in a down clue means set upright, so the word for sign is read from the bottom up

parts.note: an omen is a sign of things to come

explanation.surface: A notice is put up inside an English garden plant.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'erected' means read upwards, so the omen is turned over before going inside AN.
explanation.definitionFit: The windflower is a flowering plant of the buttercup family.

parts.note: a splash is a small dash of liquid, as of milk in tea
down can mean along, as in 'down the street'

explanation.surface: Someone hurries along to a landing, perhaps on a staircase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'landing' suggests a stair, but it is a spacecraft coming down at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A space capsule's landing in the ocean is called by this term, a specific kind of landing.

parts.note: real means actual or genuine, as something official is
an estate is a British car with a large luggage space behind the back seats

explanation.surface: A government car drives off from a country house.
explanation.walkthrough: An ESTATE car is the British name for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: Land and buildings are property, which American usage calls by this term.

definitions.meaning: in good health, as in 'I'm fine'
a shaft sunk to draw up water

explanation.surface: A spring or shaft that gives good water.
explanation.definitionFit: One word means healthy and also names a shaft dug to reach groundwater.

clue.text: Understand leg-pull about article may make one feel anxious

parts.note: to get something is to understand it
the is the definite article
a wind-up is British slang for a teasing joke, a leg-pull

explanation.surface: Getting the joke about a newspaper story might leave you nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: A WIND-UP is British slang for a tease or practical joke.
explanation.definitionFit: This British idiom means to become frightened or nervous, so it equals feeling anxious.

parts.note: to take off someone is to mimic them, to ape them

explanation.surface: Log the temperature and then take off.
explanation.definitionFit: To record sound or video onto magnetic strip, a synonym verb.

indicators.note: translated means turned into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nurse's note rendered into another language, privately.
explanation.definitionFit: This French phrase means between ourselves, said privately, so in confidence.

parts.note: a shot here is a drink, not gunfire: the farewell drink handed to a rider already mounted

explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like gunfire but is a small drink, given to riders mounted for the hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional drink served to a rider on horseback before the hunt sets off, a farewell tipple.

indicators.note: Briefly means cut short, dropping the last letter of the word for look after

parts.note: to treat a patient is to look after them
sure means certain

explanation.surface: Take good care of certain precious things for a short while.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoarded riches, gold and jewels, are valuables collectively.

clue.text: Take part in a series of motorbike time trials, then stop

parts.note: the TT, or Tourist Trophy, is the motorbike race series on the Isle of Man
to end is to stop

explanation.surface: A rider enters a set of motorbike races and then pulls up.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy motorbike races.
explanation.definitionFit: To be present at an event, as one goes to a class or meeting, is to take part in it.

clue.text: Comic play that may bring tears to your eyes?

definitions.text: that may bring tears to your eyes?
definitions.meaning: a pollen allergy that makes eyes stream

explanation.surface: A comedy so funny it makes you cry.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of Coward's comedy is also the name of the allergy to pollen that causes watery eyes.

indicators.note: cut short means docking the final letter of the game's name

parts.note: rackets is a fast indoor ball game, ancestor of squash

explanation.surface: A noisy row as a match is abandoned early.
explanation.walkthrough: RACKETS is an old British court game like squash.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud din or uproar is a clamour, a direct synonym.

parts.note: ginger here is an orange cat, and the way in is a small door it pushes through

explanation.walkthrough: 'ginger' suggests the spice in cooking, but it is a ginger cat, and 'Way in' is an entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hinged door fitted for pets is how a cat gets into the house.

clue.text: Appropriate by a rostrum to acknowledge applause

parts.note: to appropriate is to take for oneself
a rostrum was the beaked prow of a Roman warship, and a bow is a ship's prow

explanation.surface: Fitting that a speaker beside a podium should accept the cheers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rostrum' looks like a podium, but it is a ship's beaked prow.
explanation.definitionFit: Bending in thanks to the audience is how performers acknowledge applause, an idiom.

clue.text: Have in cheese and chocolate cake

indicators.note: in says the word for have is set inside the cheese

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
to own something is to have it

explanation.surface: A dessert course of cheese and a chocolate treat.
explanation.definitionFit: A dense, flat chocolate cake cut into squares is called by this name.

parts.note: fun is pleasure or enjoyment
to run an event is to organise it

explanation.surface: Someone gladly sets up a fundraiser.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponsored amateur race held to raise money for a cause is a charitable event.

clue.text: Meeting the required standard, until put out

parts.note: up to means until, as in 'up to now'
to snuff a candle is to put it out

explanation.surface: Something is good enough until it is extinguished.
explanation.definitionFit: Good enough, acceptable, of satisfactory quality: an informal idiom for meeting the required standard.

definitions.meaning: to press creases out of clothes
a club with an angled metal head

explanation.surface: A sleek club for the golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to press clothes flat and also names a metal-headed club.

clue.text: High temperature, and hard to swallow?

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
to eat is to swallow food

explanation.surface: A fever, and medicine that is hard to get down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard to swallow' reads as one phrase, but splits as H plus a verb for swallowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Hotness or warmth at a high temperature is the plain sense, a direct synonym.

parts.note: old means aged, advanced in years

explanation.surface: An elderly Tory politician who is standoffish.
explanation.definitionFit: A chilly, distant manner is unfriendly, a figurative synonym.

parts.note: to furnish is to provide or supply
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A woman named Prudence equips a newly built church.
explanation.walkthrough: Prudence looks like a woman's name but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An older sense of the word is foresight and careful planning, which is prudence.

parts.note: pop is an informal name for father

indicators.note: beginning to picks the initial letter of eat

explanation.surface: Dad starts tucking into some fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father' wants to be the definition, as the Pope is Holy Father; it is POP, and the fish is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The ruffe, a small freshwater perch, is also known by this name.

clue.text: Film guys on strike in billowing tent

indicators.note: in says the strike and the guys go inside the scrambled tent
billowing means swelling and shifting in the wind, so the letters of tent are jumbled
on says the guys come after the word for strike

parts.note: to rap is to strike sharply
men are guys

explanation.surface: Workers on strike sheltering in a tent flapping in the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'billowing' makes ENTT from TENT, and 'in' puts RAPMEN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1999 heist film starring Sean Connery and Catherine Zeta-Jones has this title.
